title: panna pipeline
about: How the football ratings and match predictions get built on GitHub Actions: four workflows. Three are started by the daily Opta scrape in the pannadata repo: the Predictions Pipeline builds the match predictions and the blog's game logs and publishes them; the Opta RAPM/SPM Pipeline refits the player ratings and publishes them; the EPV/WPA Model Training workflow scores shots and passes and publishes the xMetrics files. The Skills Seasonal Build runs weekly on its own and publishes the skill ratings tables. The pannadata repo's pipeline guide covers the scrape before these and the blog data build after them. Each workflow is timed on its own; runs are not stitched across repos.

pipelines.name: Predictions Pipeline
pipelines.about: Rebuilds the match statistics, refits the goals and outcome models, predicts every upcoming fixture, builds the blog's game logs, action equity and team strength files, then publishes everything to the predictions-latest and blog-latest releases. Only runs on the main branch that were started by the daily scrape or the weekly schedule are counted; manual and branch test runs are left out.
pipelines.triggers: The pannadata repo's daily Opta scrape sends opta-scrape-complete when it finishes; a weekly schedule (Wednesday 7pm Sydney time in summer) is the backstop. When it succeeds it sends predictions-complete to the pannadata repo, which starts the blog data build there.

stage_notes.the stages of the predictions pipeline: Each stage runs from its Step header line to the next one; stages 1 and 1c belong to the Rebuild match stats step, the rest to the Run predictions pipeline step, and the last runs to the end of its step.

stage_about.1: compute_match_stats: Skills step 01: per-90 rates and derived stats for every player-match, from the Opta player stats
stage_about.1c: keeper_style: Skills step 01c: each club's goalkeeper distribution style and each keeper's effect, used to adjust keeper stats for the club they play for
stage_about.1: build_fixture_results: Builds past results with goals and xG, and the upcoming fixtures, from the Opta lineups, events and fixtures
stage_about.1b: refresh_wc2026_squads: Rebuilds the World Cup 2026 announced-squads file from Wikipedia so expected minutes follow the latest lineups
stage_about.2: player_ratings_to_team: Turns each starting XI's player ratings into team-level features for every match
stage_about.2b: team_skill_features: Team attacking and defensive skill features from the starting XI's skill estimates at the match date
stage_about.3: team_rolling_features: Rolling form, Elo ratings and rest days per team, using only past matches
stage_about.4: build_match_dataset: Joins results, team ratings and rolling features into the match dataset, with the train, validation and test split by date
stage_about.4b: export_match_features: Writes the team-strength features the models actually use, per fixture, to a small parquet
stage_about.5: fit_goals_model: Fits the XGBoost goal-count models, one pooled and one for international matches
stage_about.6: fit_outcome_model: Fits the XGBoost home/draw/away models on top of the goals models
stage_about.7: predict_fixtures: Predicts every upcoming fixture with the fitted models
stage_about.7b: snapshot_predictions: Saves a dated copy of predictions.parquet to the predictions-history release, so past dates can be replayed with the predictions that existed then
stage_about.8: evaluate_model: Scores the models on the held-out test matches (goal errors, log-loss, accuracy, calibration)
stage_about.9: upload_predictions: Checks the predictions output is valid; it no longer uploads (step 13 does that)
stage_about.10: export_blog_data: Builds the player ratings and match predictions files for the blog, to be published in step 13
stage_about.10b: export_game_logs: Builds the per-match player value metrics (EPV, WPA and PSV) for the current season, as game_logs files
stage_about.10c: export_equity: Builds each action's EPV credit, as action_equity files the chain builder joins on
stage_about.10e: export_keeper_style: Registers the keeper style table for publishing, for the site's live keeper scorer
stage_about.11: simulate_wc2026: Simulates the 2026 World Cup (switched off once the final has been played)
stage_about.12: export_wc2026_blog: Builds the World Cup data files for the blog, including the match history and predictions
stage_about.12b: snapshot_wc_minutes: Saves a dated copy of the World Cup expected-minutes table (off after the tournament)
stage_about.12c: snapshot_wc_strength: Saves a dated copy of the World Cup team-strength table (off after the tournament)
stage_about.12f: snapshot_wc_predictions: Saves dated copies of the World Cup match probabilities (off after the tournament)
stage_about.12d: export_domestic_team_strength: Builds Tiento, the team rating, for every club, for the blog's Team Ratings page
stage_about.12e: export_cup_pairwise: Builds the knockout win-probability lookup for every Champions League, Europa League and Conference League pairing
stage_about.13: publish_release_data: The one publish: uploads the predictions and blog files to the predictions-latest and blog-latest releases, manifest last

pipelines.name: Opta RAPM/SPM Pipeline
pipelines.about: Refits the player ratings from scratch on the latest Opta data: loads and scores the events, builds splints (stretches of play between substitutions and goals), fits RAPM, SPM and xRAPM, and publishes the seasonal ratings to the ratings-data release. Only daily runs on main started by the scrape are counted; manual and branch test runs are left out.
pipelines.triggers: The pannadata repo's daily Opta scrape sends opta-scrape-complete when it finishes (the same message starts the Predictions Pipeline). It starts nothing itself: the Predictions Pipeline and the blog data build read the ratings it publishes the next time they run.

stage_notes.the stages of the rating pipeline: Each stage runs from its Step header line to the next one; the last runs to the end of the step.

stage_about.1: load_data: Loads Opta lineups, events, stats and xMetrics, scores every shot with the xG model, finds penalties and works out each match's xG for the splints
stage_about.2: data_processing: Converts the Opta tables into the processed-data form the splint builder expects
stage_about.3: splint_creation: Cuts every match into splints: stretches of play between substitutions, goals and red cards
stage_about.4: rapm: Fits the base RAPM model (ridge regression of each splint's xG on who was on the pitch)
stage_about.5: spm: Fits the SPM model: elastic net and XGBoost blended 50/50 from 80-odd player stats, plus offence and defence versions
stage_about.5b: export_spm_coefficients: Writes the SPM model's coefficients to CSV files for live scoring
stage_about.6: xrapm: Fits xRAPM: RAPM with the SPM predictions as its prior
stage_about.7: seasonal_ratings: Fits RAPM, SPM and xRAPM again for each season
stage_about.7c: team_season_strength: Builds each team's attacking and defensive strength per season from its players' xRAPM, as the opponent-quality control for later models
stage_about.8: panna_ratings: Combines xRAPM, RAPM and SPM into the final ratings table
stage_about.9: export_ratings: Uploads seasonal_xrapm.parquet and seasonal_spm.parquet to the ratings-data release (skipped on branch test runs)

pipelines.name: EPV/WPA Model Training
pipelines.about: Despite the name, the runs counted here do not retrain any model. They score every player's shots and passes with the models already published (xG and xPass), and publish the results as opta_xmetrics.parquet and opta_xmetrics_bymatch.parquet. Retraining the EPV, xG, xPass and win-probability models is only done by hand (those training steps are skipped in these runs). Counted: runs on main started by the daily scrape or the weekly schedule, at least 30 minutes long.
pipelines.triggers: The pannadata repo's daily Opta scrape sends opta-scrape-complete when it finishes (the same message starts the other two panna workflows); a weekly schedule (Monday 5am Sydney time in summer) is the backstop. It starts nothing itself: the Opta RAPM/SPM Pipeline refuses to run if opta_xmetrics.parquet is more than 14 days old, and the game logs read opta_xmetrics_bymatch.parquet.

pipelines.name: Skills Seasonal Build
pipelines.about: Rebuilds the player skills chain on a runner (it used to be run by hand): match stats, the recency-weighted RAPM target, skill features, the skill SPM and the seasonal skill ratings, then checks the new tables against the published ones and publishes them to the predictions-cache release (which the Predictions Pipeline downloads as required input). Each stage is its own job on a fresh machine, passing files on as run artifacts. Counted: weekly scheduled runs on main (only three exist so far, so fewer than 5 runs back this guide).
pipelines.triggers: GitHub's own schedule, set for Monday 3pm Sydney time in summer (4am UTC); it can also be started by hand. It starts nothing itself: the Predictions Pipeline reads the 06_seasonal_ratings.rds and psr_league_offsets.parquet it publishes.

steps.about: Checks whether any input on predictions-cache (such as the daily Opta rating caches) was republished after this chain started; fails a publishing run if so, and only warns otherwise

steps.name: Coverage gate against the published copies
steps.about: Fails if a new table has under 95% of the published rows, loses a season or most of a column's values, or keeps under 99% of the published players

steps.name: Publish to predictions-cache (safe upload)
steps.about: On scheduled runs on main: uploads the four tables to predictions-cache through a temporary name, verifying before the swap, never overwriting directly

steps.name: Say when nothing was uploaded
steps.about: Only when the run did not publish (not main, or not scheduled): says so on the run's summary page

steps.name: Post Setup R dependencies
steps.about: Clean-up for an earlier step (saves caches, removes credentials)

steps.name: Post Checkout repository
steps.about: Clean-up for an earlier step (saves caches, removes credentials)

steps.name: Complete job
steps.about: GitHub closes the job and cleans up the machine

slowest_steps.about: Runs skills step 06 (06_seasonal_skill_ratings.R): fits seasonal RAPM with the skill SPM as its prior, giving 06_seasonal_ratings.rds and the PSR league offsets

Runs skills steps 01 and 01c (data-raw/estimated-skills/run_skills_pipeline.R): each player's per-90 match stats, then each club's goalkeeper style as of each season, timed with /usr/bin/time so peak memory is recorded
Runs skills step 02 (02_estimate_skills.R): decay-weighted skill estimates, one row per player per season, saved as 02_skill_features.rds
Installs the R packages the stage needs (devtools, arrow, dplyr, data.table and others), from a cache when it can
Runs skills step 03 (03_skill_spm.R): fits the SPM on the skill features against the decayed RAPM target, saved as 03_skill_spm.rds and its as-of version
